steps.title: Dashboard shows live freshness indicators
steps.narration: The dashboard loads with a green Ready badge in the top-right. A small gray label next to it updates every second to show data freshness — this is new behavior that continuously updates rather than freezing. The green GO banner below also has a live freshness label.
steps.point_out: The Ready badge with its freshness label ('as of Ns ago') in the top-right. The GO banner below the header with its own freshness label in parentheses.

steps.title: Data page maintains freshness visibility
steps.narration: Navigate to the Data page. The Ready badge and freshness labels appear here too — they work consistently across every page of the app.
steps.point_out: The Ready badge and freshness label in the header, and the GO banner below. The SNAPSHOT dates count on this page.

steps.title: Backtest shows historical evidence scorecard
steps.narration: The Backtest page displays historical performance data across multiple time horizons. The ready badge remains visible in the header, confirming the data is current.
steps.point_out: The scorecard showing return and risk metrics (1d, 5d, 10d, etc.). Notice the Ready badge with freshness label in the header.

steps.title: Background compute work is transparently disclosed
steps.narration: Request a historical date that needs fresh computation. When the app does heavy work, a 'background compute running' indicator appears in the header alongside the Ready badge, showing you when the system is actively computing.
steps.point_out: The 'background compute running (N)' chip in the header showing real-time work in progress.

steps.title: Data page shows live computation progress details
steps.narration: The Data page displays a live progress row whenever background compute is running. It shows the as-of date, elapsed time, and horizon completion counts so you can monitor active work in real time.
steps.point_out: The background compute progress row with elapsed time and horizon details (e.g., 'elapsed Xs/1m27s · horizons 0/5→3/5').
